user.title: Hauswacht
user.description: Set up the Hauswacht intrusion alarm. The alarm starts disarmed. Sirens are not controlled in this version.

init.description: {saved}Every change is saved as soon as you submit the form; you then return to the menu.

code.title: PIN rules
code.description:
Users with a PIN: {pin_users}.

**Master PIN:** a simple PIN without separate users, e.g. so voice assistants (Alexa) can only disarm with a PIN. It also appears in the user list as “Master-PIN”.

As soon as a PIN exists, the panel requires it to disarm. With “Allow dashboard buttons despite PIN”, the dashboard buttons “Disarm now” and “End alarm” keep working – only logged-in Home Assistant users can reach them anyway.

⚠️ **Important:** As soon as **one** PIN exists, the panel (and Alexa) require a PIN to disarm – **from everyone**. People without a PIN can then only disarm via dashboard buttons (if allowed under PIN rules) or the push button. So: give everyone a PIN (shared PIN allowed) or no one.

zones.title: Sensor groups
zones.description:
{saved}A **sensor group** is a group of sensors that are always monitored together – for example:

- **Perimeter**: all door and window contacts (with their tamper sensors)
- **Inside** or **Basement**: motion and presence sensors

In the **profiles** you then choose which sensor groups are armed: "Home" = perimeter only, "Away" = perimeter and inside.

Every sensor belongs to **exactly one** sensor group. Hauswacht only monitors sensors that are in a sensor group.

zone_add.title: Add sensor group
zone_add.description:
Select all sensors that belong to this sensor group. How a sensor triggers (door with entry delay, window instantly, motion, tamper) is derived from its device class – exceptions under System settings → Sensor behaviour.

Each sensor can only be in **one** sensor group.

data_description.label: Handy for many sensors: put the label directly on the sensor entity (not the device); new sensors with the label then belong to the sensor group automatically.

infrastructure.title: Monitor radio networks and gateways
infrastructure.description:
Select sensors that report whether a radio network or gateway is running – e.g. the connection state of the Zigbee2MQTT bridge or an MQTT broker. If such a system fails, all sensors behind it can no longer report. Hauswacht reports the fault and treats arming as with unavailable sensors.

For sensors of type “problem”, “on” means fault; for all others “on” means OK.

sirens.description: Register the sirens Hauswacht may use for intrusion alarms. Fire safety: Hauswacht never switches a siren on or off while any smoke detector reports fire, or while the fire state of a registered siren is unknown. Siren control stays LOCKED until you enable it here and confirm.

homecoming.description: Hauswacht records when entry doors open and people are detected as home – per location source – and calculates whether automatic homecoming would be reliable. The observation switches NOTHING: no disarm, no alarm. Press “Homecoming report” for the report.

rules.title: Trigger rules
rules.description:
{saved}A **trigger rule** triggers only on a **sequence** of sensors – e.g. “front door, then basement within 120 s”. The door alone or the basement alone then trigger nothing.

How a trigger rule works:
- It consists of **steps** that must happen **one after another**. Step 2 only counts once step 1 is fulfilled – and only within the time set at step 1.
- In each step you pick sensors and decide when **this step** is fulfilled: one of them (OR), all of them in any order (AND) or at least N different ones.
- When the last step is fulfilled, there is an alarm – immediately or after the entry delay.

Each alarm profile chooses which trigger rules apply. One fulfilled trigger rule is enough.

**Existing trigger rules:**
{rules}

menu_options.rule_yaml_add: New trigger rule as YAML (expert mode)

rule_delete.description: The trigger rule is also removed from all alarm profiles.

rule_meta.title: Trigger rule: name and result
rule_meta.description: Name the trigger rule and decide what happens when all steps are fulfilled. You add the steps one by one afterwards.

rule_step.title: Step {step}
rule_step.description:
**So far:** {rule_text}

Pick the sensors of this step and when **this step** is fulfilled. The setting only applies to this step. The next step only counts afterwards – that creates the order. Whatever may happen in any order belongs in **one** step with “all of them”.

data.zones: Sensor groups (any sensor of the group)

data_description.within: From the moment this step is fulfilled, the next step has this much time. Irrelevant for the last step. For “all” or “at least N” in the first step also: how close its sensors must be.

triggering.title: Alarm triggering
triggering.description:
{saved}What triggers an alarm?

- **Sensor groups** bundle sensors that belong together (e.g. doors, windows, basement).
- **Trigger rules** only trigger on a sequence of sensors (e.g. “door, then basement”).

In each **alarm profile** you choose which sensor groups trigger alone and which trigger rules apply.

menu_options.zones: Sensor groups – which sensors belong together

rule_unless.title: Not if before …
rule_unless.description:
**So far:** {rule_text}

The trigger rule does **not** apply if one of these sensors triggered within the given time **before step 1** – e.g. someone already moving around inside who then opens a window is no burglar. Affects this trigger rule only. Deselect everything = remove the exception.

data.zones: Sensor groups (any sensor of the group)

rule_yaml.title: Trigger rule as YAML
rule_yaml.description:
Expert mode: the whole trigger rule as YAML. Sensor groups by name (`group: Basement`), sensors by entity ID (`sensor: binary_sensor.x`).

- Steps: `any: [...]` (one of), `all: [...]` (all), `count: 2` + `of: [...]` (at least N), nestable; `within:` time until the next step.
- `result:` alarm, entry_delay or notify (notification only).
- `unless:` expression + `before:` seconds – not if that happened within this time before step 1.
- `conditions:` list: `time` (after/before/weekdays), `person` (entity, in: home/not_home/zone.x), `state` (entity, is), `numeric` (entity, above/below, attribute), `and`/`or`/`not`. Not evaluable = met.

Examples are in the documentation.

users_without_pin.title: Hauswacht: not everyone has a PIN
users_without_pin.description:
As soon as a PIN exists, the panel (and Alexa) require it **from everyone** to disarm. These people have no PIN and cannot disarm there: **{people}**.

Options:
- Give them a PIN under Hauswacht → Configure → System settings → Users and PINs (a shared family PIN is allowed), or
- enable “Allow dashboard buttons despite PIN” under PIN rules (currently: {buttons}) – dashboard buttons and the push button then keep working without a PIN.

Scheduled profiles and presence automation are not affected.
